paragraphs: Drawing organ boundaries in CT scans takes substantial expert time, which constrains the size and variety of medical segmentation datasets. This paper introduces an active learning annotation procedure and uses it to produce AbdomenAtlas-8K: 8,448 CT volumes containing 3.2 million slices, with annotations covering eight abdominal organs and structures.

The procedure combines predictions from multiple pretrained segmentation models to reduce label bias. It then detects prediction errors and directs annotators toward the most salient corrections. This makes human attention a targeted part of the workflow: model predictions provide a starting point, while error detection helps determine where correction effort should go.

The authors report completing annotation in three weeks while maintaining similar or better annotation quality. Their estimate for conventional annotation reaches 1,600 weeks for an experienced annotator, so the comparison concerns a major change in workflow. They also organize common mistakes by algorithms and annotators into a taxonomy, providing a basis for improving both predictions and subsequent human corrections.
neurips-2023-abdomenatlas-8k-annotating-.tldr: An active learning workflow combines model predictions and targeted human corrections to annotate 8,448 abdominal CT volumes in three weeks.

paragraphs: Black-box optimization searches for good solutions using function evaluations when gradients are unavailable. Finite-difference methods estimate gradients by comparing evaluations along selected directions. Nonsmooth functions complicate this strategy because a conventional gradient may not exist, and practical black-box settings may offer no way to verify smoothness assumptions.

The paper introduces O-ZD, which combines a smooth approximation of the objective with a structured choice of probing directions. Specifically, it uses a subset of random orthogonal directions and proves that the resulting estimates approximate the gradient of the smoothed function. The contribution extends the analysis of structured finite differences beyond the previously studied smooth setting.

The guarantees depend on the objective class. For nonsmooth convex functions, O-ZD achieves optimal complexity. For nonsmooth nonconvex functions, the analysis bounds the iterations required to control the expected size of the smoothed gradient. It also recovers smooth convex results and extends them to smooth nonconvex problems. Numerical simulations satisfying the assumptions show strong practical performance.
neurips-2023-an-optimal-structured-zerot.tldr: O-ZD uses random orthogonal finite-difference directions to optimize nonsmooth black-box functions, achieving optimal complexity in the convex setting.

paragraphs: ImageNet errors are difficult to interpret because incorrect or ambiguous labels can make reasonable predictions count as failures. Revised labels and evaluation protocols have already placed leading models above 95% accuracy, motivating closer examination of the errors that remain. Manually assigning error categories requires experts and is difficult to repeat consistently.

This paper introduces an automated framework for classifying model errors and applies it to more than 900 models. Categorizing mistakes makes it possible to examine how architecture, model scale, and pretraining data relate to the distribution of error types, rather than reducing every evaluation to a single count of correct predictions.

Across the models studied, top-1 accuracy strongly predicts the proportion of each error type. In particular, severe mistakes form a substantially smaller share of errors as accuracy rises. This gives top-1 accuracy a qualified endorsement: label problems mean it can understate actual performance, but its association with error severity makes it informative about progress beyond the raw score itself.
neurips-2023-automated-classification-of.tldr: Automated analysis of over 900 ImageNet models finds that higher top-1 accuracy predicts a smaller proportion of severe errors.

paragraphs: Sensitivity measures how important an individual data point is for preserving a regression problem when the dataset is reduced. Sampling according to these importance measures supports approximation guarantees. Efficient sensitivity estimation was previously available for the ell-2 setting, where the quantities are known as leverage scores; this paper develops algorithms for broader ell-p settings.

The authors establish an equivalence between approximate sensitivity computation and approximate regression. They then give algorithms for individual sensitivities, their sum, and their maximum. For an n-by-d matrix, an alpha approximation of ell-1 sensitivities costs n/alpha sensitivity computations. Estimating total ell-p sensitivity to a constant factor requires roughly the square root of d such computations, with no polynomial dependence on n.

These results separate the cost of obtaining useful summary information from computing every sensitivity individually. Experiments on structured matrices from real datasets show that total sensitivity can be estimated quickly and is substantially below theoretical predictions. The observed gap supports the authors' conclusion that these datasets have relatively low effective dimensionality on average.
neurips-2023-computing-approximate-ell-p.tldr: New algorithms efficiently approximate ell-p data sensitivities and their summaries, extending importance estimation beyond ell-2 leverage scores.

paragraphs: Spatio-temporal graph forecasting predicts how quantities evolve across connected locations or entities. Two difficulties arise when the temporal conditions encountered at prediction time differ from training and when causal influences between connected entities change. The paper introduces CaST, a framework that addresses these challenges through an explicit causal account of graph data generation.

CaST begins with a structural causal model describing the relationships involved in generating observations. To address temporal distribution changes, it combines back-door adjustment with a disentanglement block that separates temporal environments from input data. For spatial causation, it combines front-door adjustment with edge-level convolution to represent how causal effects propagate through graph connections.

The approach matters because it gives the temporal and spatial components distinct roles tied to the proposed causal model. Experiments on three real-world datasets find that CaST consistently outperforms the existing methods evaluated and offers good interpretability. These findings support the usefulness of its causal treatments for the forecasting settings studied, including changing temporal conditions and dynamic spatial influence.
neurips-2023-deciphering-spatio-temporal.tldr: CaST uses causal adjustments to address temporal distribution shifts and changing spatial influences in graph forecasting.

paragraphs: Decorate3D provides a workflow for changing the appearance of real-world 3D objects represented from images. It first models an object with a neural radiance field, then separates that representation into an explicit mesh, a view-dependent texture, and a diffuse UV texture. This decomposition gives users an editable surface representation.

Users can modify the UV texture manually or supply text describing a desired appearance. For automatic generation, the method uses structure-aware score distillation sampling to optimize a neural UV texture. The purpose is to make an image diffusion model produce texture that remains consistent across the object's 3D surface, connecting text-driven image generation with mesh decoration.

A further training procedure resamples a small number of views, and a super-resolution model refines the resulting UV texture to 2048 by 2048 pixels. The experiments report superior performance in retexturing real-world objects. Together, the components address both coherent appearance across views and fine texture detail, while retaining a route for direct manual editing.
neurips-2023-decorate3d-text-driven-high.tldr: Decorate3D turns image-based object representations into editable meshes and generates high-resolution, 3D-consistent textures from text.

paragraphs: A graph can contain nodes whose neighbors are mostly similar to them and nodes whose neighbors are mostly different. These are homophilic and heterophilic local patterns, respectively. The paper argues that treating an entire graph as one type can obscure important differences in how well a graph neural network classifies individual nodes.

The authors find that GNNs typically perform well on homophilic nodes in homophilic graphs and heterophilic nodes in heterophilic graphs, while struggling with nodes showing the opposite local pattern. They investigate this disparity both theoretically and empirically, shifting attention from graph-wide performance to the relationship between local structure and prediction quality.

Their analysis develops a PAC-Bayesian generalization bound that accommodates non-independent, non-identically distributed data. It identifies aggregated feature distance and differences in homophily ratios between training and testing nodes as explanations for the disparity. The authors use these findings to explain the effectiveness of deeper GNNs and identify an overlooked source of distribution shift, motivating a new graph out-of-distribution scenario.
neurips-2023-demystifying-structural-dis.tldr: GNN performance varies with local node structure, and a new generalization analysis links this disparity to training–testing differences.

paragraphs: Research on visual emergent communication studies how agents learn to convey information through sketches. This paper focuses on a feature that earlier work overlooked: communication can unfold through multiple rounds of interaction. It introduces Interactive Sketch Question Answering, a task in which two cooperating players exchange sketches to answer a question about an image.

The authors design an interactive communication system for this task and assess it along three dimensions: answer accuracy, drawing complexity, and human interpretability. Considering these together makes the task more demanding than simply producing a correct answer. The sketches also need to communicate efficiently and remain understandable to people.

The experiments show that multiple rounds of interaction facilitate targeted, efficient communication between the agents. The system achieves an effective balance among the three evaluation factors. The contribution is therefore both a task for studying interactive visual communication and a system demonstrating its usefulness. It supplies evidence that the opportunity to interact can shape how agents communicate relevant visual information.
neurips-2023-emergent-communication-in-i.tldr: A sketch-based question-answering task shows that multiple interaction rounds help agents communicate accurately, efficiently, and interpretably.

paragraphs: Phylogenetic inference uses molecular data and evolutionary models to estimate relationships among species. Uncertainty concerns both the branching arrangement of the evolutionary tree and the evolutionary distances along its branches. Accounting for these alternatives matters when drawing conclusions or averaging over possible trees, but the number of branching arrangements creates a difficult computational problem.

GeoPhy introduces a fully differentiable formulation by representing distributions over tree topologies in continuous geometric spaces. This provides a way to use gradient-based variational Bayesian inference without restricting the set of candidate topologies. The method also considers the choice of design space and uses control variates in gradient estimation to support practical optimization.

On real benchmark datasets, GeoPhy significantly outperforms the other approximate Bayesian methods evaluated that also consider the full topology space. The result supports continuous geometric representation as a useful route to approximate inference over evolutionary trees. Its central contribution is enabling optimization across unrestricted topological candidates while maintaining a formulation designed to account for uncertainty.
neurips-2023-geophy-differentiable-phylo.tldr: GeoPhy represents tree-topology distributions geometrically to enable differentiable Bayesian inference without restricting candidate evolutionary trees.

paragraphs: Neural implicit representations can support 3D scene segmentation using only 2D supervision, but existing approaches require costly optimization for each scene. GNeSF addresses this obstacle by building a segmentation framework that can handle new scenes at inference. It conditions its representation on image features and semantic maps from multiple views, rather than relying only on spatial information.

For each 3D point, a soft voting mechanism combines semantic information from different images. Image features and differences between views determine the voting weights, allowing nearby views to contribute more than distant ones. A visibility module detects occluded views and filters out information that could harm the combined prediction.

This design connects 3D predictions to transferable image evidence while accounting for viewpoint and visibility. With only 2D semantic supervision, the framework can produce semantic maps and segment previously unseen 3D scenes. Experiments show performance comparable to methods optimized for individual scenes, and the approach can even outperform existing methods using stronger supervision. These findings support generalizable segmentation without expensive per-scene fitting.
neurips-2023-gnesf-generalizable-neural-.tldr: GNeSF combines semantic evidence across visible camera views to segment new 3D scenes using only 2D supervision.

paragraphs: Pairwise relationships can leave out dependencies that involve larger groups of variables. This matters for complex multivariate data, where understanding each pair separately may not describe the full statistical structure. The paper develops measures and statistical tests for interactions involving d variables, with d at least two.

The proposed measures form a hierarchy that accounts for increasingly broad possibilities for splitting the joint probability distribution into factors. Nonparametric kernel tests then assess whether interactions at a chosen order are statistically significant. This connects the definition of an interaction with a systematic procedure for testing it from data.

The authors use lattice theory to explain how the measures and their composite permutation tests are constructed. They also connect simplicial complexes with kernel matrix centering and use these mathematical relationships to improve computational efficiency. Numerical validation on synthetic data and an application to neuroimaging illustrate the framework. The contribution combines a structured account of higher-order dependence with practical tools for determining whether such dependence is supported by observations.
neurips-2023-interaction-measures-partit.tldr: A hierarchy of interaction measures and kernel tests detects statistically significant dependencies involving groups of variables.

paragraphs: Before a language model processes text, a tokenizer converts it into an encoded sequence. This paper shows that this step can treat languages unevenly even before the model generates an answer. Translations of the same text can produce drastically different sequence lengths, reaching a factor of 15 in some cases.

The disparity persists for tokenizers deliberately trained to support multiple languages. Moving to character-level or byte-level representations does not eliminate the issue: the authors find encoding-length differences exceeding a factor of four for some language pairs. The problem therefore extends beyond a simple distinction between multilingual and other tokenizers.

Different encoding lengths have consequences for access costs, processing time, latency, and how much content fits into a model's context. Equivalent content can consume very different amounts of the resources available to users across language communities. The authors consequently advocate training future models with multilingually fair subword tokenizers. Their findings identify the text representation itself as a consequential part of multilingual fairness.
neurips-2023-language-model-tokenizers-i.tldr: Tokenization can make equivalent text up to 15 times longer across languages, creating disparities in costs, latency, and usable context.

paragraphs: This paper studies federated learning where isolated clients hold different data distributions and can reach a server only through wireless links in an environment without fixed infrastructure. The proposed personalized learning approach incorporates server mobility, allowing learning to proceed as the server moves randomly toward clients.

The optimization algorithm, RWSADMM, uses hard inequality constraints to express local proximity among adjacent clients. This provides a way to relate personalized local solutions without requiring consensus updates or imposing a regularization penalty that introduces bias. A stochastic solver works with an approximated optimization problem to reduce the computation required from clients.

The authors provide a stationary-point convergence guarantee for the solver, stated in terms of almost-sure convergence in expectation. Their theoretical and empirical results also report fast convergence, substantial accuracy improvements over the evaluated baselines, reduced communication costs, and improved scalability. The contribution links a mobile communication setting with constrained personalization, addressing both uneven client data and the practical cost of participating in distributed learning.
neurips-2023-mobilizing-personalized-fed.tldr: RWSADMM supports personalized federated learning through a moving server, local inequality constraints, and a computationally efficient stochastic solver.

paragraphs: Mutual information measures statistical dependence, but estimating it becomes difficult when the variables have many dimensions. Slicing methods make the problem more manageable by projecting high-dimensional variables into one-dimensional spaces. The paper examines a weakness of choosing these projection directions uniformly: the projections can discard features that carry important dependence information.

The authors propose searching for an optimal distribution over slicing directions. This changes the focus from treating directions equally to determining how slices should be distributed for the information measure. They investigate theoretical questions about this optimization and develop analyses that support the proposed framework.

A practical algorithm connects the theoretical results with modern machine learning frameworks. Across benchmark-domain experiments, the resulting information measure shows significant gains over the state-of-the-art baselines evaluated. The contribution treats the choice of projection distribution as a central part of measuring dependence. It preserves the computational motivation for reducing dimensionality while addressing the information loss associated with uniformly selected directions.
neurips-2023-on-slicing-optimality-for-m.tldr: Learning a distribution of projection directions improves sliced mutual-information measurement over uniformly chosen slices in benchmark experiments.

paragraphs: Social networks recommend connections that users are likely to find relevant, but new connections can also change polarization and disagreement. This paper asks whether relevance and conflict reduction tend to align. It studies that relationship using the Friedkin-Johnsen model of opinion dynamics, which supplies the framework for analyzing how network changes affect opinions.

The authors first analyze how adding links changes opinion conflict and relate the size of that change to structural properties of the links. They then characterize the gap between links selected to maximize conflict reduction and links selected for relevance. Real-world data and 13 recommendation algorithms provide different operational definitions of relevance for measuring this gap.

The findings show that some more accurate recommendation algorithms also produce better conflict reduction, although this does not hold for all of them. Relevance therefore need not oppose conflict reduction in the settings studied. The results suggest that engagement-oriented connection recommendations may be less conflict-provoking than commonly assumed, while leaving an important role for the particular recommendation algorithm.
neurips-2023-on-the-relationship-between.tldr: Under an opinion-dynamics model, some more accurate social-link recommenders also reduce conflict more effectively, but the relationship is not universal.

paragraphs: Choosing learning rates, momentum, or an optimization method can itself create a nonconvex optimization problem. This makes global guarantees difficult for conventional iterative tuning approaches. The paper considers the broader problem of meta-optimization: learning an optimization algorithm online from the problem instances encountered.

The authors formulate meta-optimization as an optimal control problem. They use convex relaxation techniques within a nonstochastic control framework to address the nonconvexity of choosing an optimizer. This gives control theory an active role in learning optimization behavior, extending beyond its use for studying whether an existing optimization process is stable.

The resulting guarantees compare the learned method with the best offline choice from a specified class of methods. Expressed as regret guarantees, they establish convergence comparable to that of the best method selected with hindsight. The comparison class is central to the claim: the result concerns competition with those candidate methods. This provides a theoretical basis for adapting optimization online while retaining a meaningful retrospective performance benchmark.
neurips-2023-online-control-for-meta-opt.tldr: Formulating optimizer selection as online control yields regret guarantees against the best optimization method in a specified class.

paragraphs: OpenIllumination is a dataset for evaluating methods that infer scene properties from images, including inverse rendering and material decomposition. It contains more than 108,000 images of 64 real objects with varied materials. The objects are captured from 72 camera views under many different lighting conditions.

Each image comes with accurate camera parameters, ground-truth illumination, and a foreground segmentation mask. These annotations supply information about how the image was captured and which pixels belong to the object. The combination of viewpoint variation, lighting variation, and accompanying annotations provides a basis for quantitative evaluation on real objects.

The authors use the dataset to examine several state-of-the-art inverse rendering methods and compare their performance. Its main contribution is the evaluation resource: varied real-object observations paired with known capture information allow methods to be assessed in a shared setting. The dataset is intended to support most inverse rendering and material decomposition approaches, and the authors make both the dataset and code available.
neurips-2023-openillumination-a-multi-il.tldr: OpenIllumination provides over 108,000 annotated images of real objects under varied views and lighting for evaluating inverse rendering.

paragraphs: Conditional score-based diffusion models generate target data using conditioning examples, but their usual training setup requires paired data. Such pairs may be scarce or unavailable. OTCS addresses both partially paired and unpaired datasets by using optimal transport to estimate a coupling: a relationship connecting examples across the source and target distributions.

The method constructs this relationship with L2-regularized optimal transport, using an unsupervised formulation for unpaired data and a semi-supervised formulation when some pairs exist. It then generalizes the paired diffusion training objective to these settings. A compatibility-based resampling strategy selects examples that fit the estimated relationship well and uses them as training guidance.

Experiments on unpaired super-resolution and semi-paired image translation demonstrate the method's effectiveness. The authors also prove, with a theoretical bound, that OTCS realizes the data transport described by optimal transport. This connects the generation procedure to the estimated distributional relationship and offers an approach to transporting data across distributions at the scale that motivates the work.
neurips-2023-optimal-transport-guided-co.tldr: OTCS uses optimal-transport couplings and compatibility-based sampling to train conditional diffusion models with partially paired or unpaired data.

paragraphs: Large collections of user preferences for generated images are often held by companies and unavailable to other researchers. This paper introduces a web application where people generate images from text and indicate their preferences. The resulting open dataset, Pick-a-Pic, contains prompts and real users' judgments about generated images.

The authors use these data to train PickScore, a CLIP-based function that scores images according to predicted human preference. On the evaluated preference-prediction task, it achieves performance described as superhuman. That finding concerns predicting preference judgments, giving the scoring function a specific role in assessing how people are likely to respond to generated images.

When used to evaluate generation models, PickScore correlates more closely with human rankings than the other automatic metrics tested. The authors consequently recommend it for model evaluation and recommend Pick-a-Pic prompts as more relevant than MS-COCO prompts for this purpose. They also demonstrate that ranking generated outputs with PickScore can enhance existing text-to-image systems.
neurips-2023-pick-a-pic-an-open-dataset-.tldr: Pick-a-Pic collects open user-preference data that enables PickScore to evaluate and rank generated images in closer agreement with human judgments.

paragraphs: This paper investigates what attention layers can represent efficiently compared with other neural architectures. It focuses on architectural resources such as width, depth, and embedding dimension. By constructing tasks with provable complexity requirements, the authors identify both advantages and limitations of transformer representations.

For a sparse averaging task, recurrent and feedforward networks require complexity that grows polynomially with input size, while transformers need only logarithmic growth. The same construction establishes the necessity and role of a large embedding dimension. The advantage therefore comes with an architectural requirement that helps explain how attention realizes the task efficiently.

A triple detection task gives the contrasting result: attention requires complexity growing linearly with input size. The authors also identify natural variants that attention can solve efficiently, qualifying the reach of this difficult example. Their proofs use communication complexity to reason about information processing within these architectures. Together, the results provide task-specific mathematical explanations of where attention offers substantial representational savings and where its resource requirements grow.
neurips-2023-representational-strengths-.tldr: Provable task comparisons show major representational advantages for attention on sparse averaging and limitations on triple detection.

paragraphs: Gaussian processes provide predictions with uncertainty, but their computations require solving linear systems that generally have cubic cost in dataset size and can be sensitive to poor conditioning. This paper explores stochastic gradient methods for approximately solving those systems, with the aim of making posterior sampling more computationally efficient.

The authors design low-variance optimization objectives for posterior sampling and extend them to inducing-point methods. They investigate why stochastic gradient descent can produce accurate predictions even when optimization converges slowly. A spectral analysis characterizes the implicit bias caused by stopping before convergence and explains how incomplete optimization affects predictions.

The analysis shows that predictive distributions remain close to the true posterior in regions with sufficient data coverage and regions sufficiently far from the data. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance on regression tasks that are sufficiently large or ill-conditioned. On a large-scale Bayesian optimization task, the uncertainty estimates match those of substantially more expensive baselines, supporting the practical value of approximate solves in these settings.
neurips-2023-sampling-from-gaussian-proc.tldr: Stochastic gradient descent can efficiently approximate Gaussian-process posterior samples while preserving accurate predictive uncertainty in the studied settings.

paragraphs: Dataset pruning removes training data to reduce computation while preserving useful performance. This paper studies pruning specifically for transfer learning, where a model first learns from a source dataset and then is fine-tuned on downstream target tasks. The question is which source data can be removed without harming those later tasks.

The authors find that existing pruning methods are unsuitable for this transfer setting and approach selection through the relationship between source and target domains. They propose label mapping for supervised pretraining and feature mapping for self-supervised pretraining. These methods make downstream relevance part of the decision about which source data to retain.

Across numerous transfer-learning tasks, the experiments show source-class pruning of up to 40–80% without sacrificing downstream performance, alongside pretraining speedups of two to five times. These are reported experimental outcomes rather than guarantees for every source–target combination. The approach also applies to costly transfer techniques such as adversarial pretraining, showing how target-aware data selection can reduce effort across more than one pretraining setup.
neurips-2023-selectivity-drives-producti.tldr: Source–target mapping guides dataset pruning that preserves downstream accuracy while delivering reported pretraining speedups of two to five times.

paragraphs: Gaussian processes produce uncertainty estimates, but those estimates can be miscalibrated and lack frequentist guarantees. Existing calibration approaches enlarge the posterior variance, which can make predictive intervals excessively broad. The paper addresses the challenge of producing uncertainty estimates that satisfy calibration requirements while remaining tight enough to be informative.

The proposed method generates predictive quantiles using a computation inspired by ordinary Gaussian-process posterior variance. It introduces a different set of hyperparameters chosen to satisfy an empirical calibration constraint. This creates more flexibility than variance inflation alone, and the authors optimize that flexibility to obtain tight predictive quantiles.

The paper establishes calibration under reasonable assumptions and reports better sharpness than existing approaches in calibrated regression. Here, sharpness concerns how tightly the predictions express uncertainty, so the improvement addresses the loss of precision that can accompany calibration. The central contribution is a way to adjust uncertainty through a flexible constrained computation, with both a conditional calibration result and empirical evidence of tighter predictions.
neurips-2023-sharp-calibrated-gaussian-p.tldr: A flexible Gaussian-process calibration method learns predictive quantiles that satisfy calibration constraints while improving sharpness.

paragraphs: In-context learning lets a language model respond to task examples placed in its input without changing its weights. This paper gives the phenomenon a theoretical framework based on probably approximately correct learning. The framework supports finite-sample complexity results, addressing how much example data is needed for the analyzed learning setup.

The model has two stages: pretraining fits a function to a distribution, and the in-context stage holds that function fixed while adding downstream examples to its input. Under mild assumptions, the authors prove efficient in-context learnability when pretraining data come from a mixture of latent tasks. This holds even though the resulting input differs substantially from the pretraining distribution.

The analysis indicates that, in this setting, the examples primarily help identify which task is being requested. This explains how useful adaptation can occur with unchanged weights: pretraining has already established the relevant task structure. The conclusion is specific to the analyzed latent-task setting and agrees with empirical findings cited by the authors, providing a theoretical basis for understanding this form of adaptation.
neurips-2023-the-learnability-of-in-cont.tldr: A PAC framework proves efficient in-context learning under latent-task assumptions and explains it primarily as identifying the task.

paragraphs: A learned regression model can serve as a control variate to reduce the variance of a Monte Carlo estimate. This paper asks when that strategy improves convergence. It studies estimation of moments of a Sobolev function from observations at random quadrature nodes, providing a mathematical setting for examining smoothness and rare extreme values.

The authors first establish an information-theoretic lower bound that defines the best achievable rate for the problem. They then analyze a quadrature rule using a nonparametric regression-adjusted control variate. Under a sufficient smoothness assumption, this rule improves on the Monte Carlo rate and reaches the minimax optimal rate.

The Sobolev Embedding Theorem explains an important implication of that assumption: it rules out rare and extreme events. When such events are present in the analyzed setting, the control variate cannot improve the convergence rate, while a truncated Monte Carlo algorithm can attain the minimax rate. The findings therefore connect the value of regression adjustment to the function class and its allowance for extreme behavior.
neurips-2023-when-can-regression-adjuste.tldr: Regression-based control variates achieve optimal Monte Carlo improvements under sufficient smoothness, while rare extremes favor truncation in the analyzed setting.
